question: Which of the following drug is contraindicated in a patient of myasthenia gravis: September 2008
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Succinylcholine" -> "depolarizing neuromuscular blocker" -> "exacerbates muscle weakness" -> "contraindicated in myasthenia gravis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Tubocurare" -> "non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker" -> "increased muscle weakness" -> "contraindicated in myasthenia gravis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pyridostigmine" -> "acetylcholinesterase inhibitor" -> "improves neuromuscular transmission" -> "used in myasthenia gravis" -> "not contraindicated" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Halothane" -> "general anesthetic" -> "no direct effect on neuromuscular junction" -> "not contraindicated in myasthenia gravis" -> 80%
analysis: In patients with myasthenia gravis, the use of neuromuscular blockers must be carefully considered due to their potential to exacerbate muscle weakness. Succinylcholine, a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker, is contraindicated because it can cause prolonged muscle paralysis and worsen the condition. Tubocurare, a non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker, is generally avoided but not as strongly contraindicated as succinylcholine. Pyridostigmine is used to treat myasthenia gravis by improving neuromuscular transmission, so it is not contraindicated. Halothane, a general anesthetic, does not directly affect the neuromuscular junction and is not contraindicated. Based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, succinylcholine is the most likely drug to be contraindicated in myasthenia gravis.
